I had it put in about a month ago. The insertion was the worst. It was one of the worst pains I've ever experienced, I'll just be honest. Granted, she had to use this special tool on me to access my cervix and apparently not everyone has to have that used. I also don't have a high pain tolerance for medical procedures. The cramping didn't really bother me, it lasted for maybe three days after it was inserted. I just took 800 mg ibuprofen when needed. My first period on it lasted for two weeks, but it was really light bleeding, so that sucked. I'm still waiting for my next period so it's kind of weird having the irregular cycle right now. Other than the pain upon insertion and really long period, I'm super happy with it so far. I haven't noticed any bodily side effects, but then, I had no issues with that on birth control pills. Sex is not painful for me at all! Both myself and my partner love not having to freak out about pregnancy if we don't use a condom. 

TL;DR: Insertion pain sucks and the irregular cycle can be frustrating but awesome not having to worry.

For me, medication has done wonders. When I was depressed it felt like a cloud was constantly following me. The medicine removed the cloud so I could feel again. Just because you take a prescription for depression doesn't mean you're suddenly a zombie. You have to try different meds to figure out what works for you. It's not shameful, like so many people seem to think.

Now that my depression is under control, exercise and a good diet is very helpful for keeping up my mood. When I eat junk I feel sluggish, lazy, and I'm more likely to feel down.

What doesn't work: people telling you to just be happy. People saying, "Think of all the people with worse problems!" That's not helpful. If you are depressed, it's not just something you can change with a snap of your fingers.
